uedcli:
usage: uedcli [-h] [--project PROJECT]
              {actor,brush,mover,level,event,project,class,sound,music,stash,prefab,docs,texture,substrate,cache}
              ...

uedcli CLI — the LLM-facing verb surface. Query and mutate verbs operate
model-side on $UEDCLI_LEVEL's git-native T3D trunk (`maps/<level>/`); the
editor is reached only via a per-command ephemeral spin-up (materialize /
preview / the stash CSG generators). The project's OWN git is the history —
uedcli reads it but never runs git for you, so history/recovery exist only
once the project is its own repo (`level status` reports when it is not).

positional arguments:
  {actor,brush,mover,level,event,project,class,sound,music,stash,prefab,docs,texture,substrate,cache}
    actor               actor query/mutate verbs
    brush               brush geometry verbs
    mover               mover (animated brush actor) keyframe verbs
    level               level lifecycle verbs (create/import/reimport/list/mat
                        erialize/preview/status/doctor)
    event               analyse the level's Tag<->Event trigger wiring (who-
                        triggers-whom). Offline, model-side, no editor. Sub-
                        verbs: graph
    project             inspect the resolved uedcli project
    class               discover the substrate's actor classes and their
                        property schemas (offline; reads the game's own .u
                        packages — no editor, no level needed)
    sound               discover and classify the substrate's sound objects
                        (offline; reads the game's own packages — no editor,
                        no level needed)
    music               discover and classify the substrate's music objects
                        (offline; reads the game's own packages — no editor,
                        no level needed)
    stash               capture/replay named actor sets (private register);
                        edit a stored one in place with any content verb +
                        --tree stash/<id>
    prefab              the durable shared prefab library (tier 2); edit a
                        stored one in place with any content verb + --tree
                        prefab/<name>
    docs                read uedcli's own user documentation (the CLI
                        reference and the level-design guides) without leaving
                        the terminal
    texture             discover, view and classify the substrate's textures
                        (offline; decodes the game's own .utx/.u packages — no
                        editor, no level needed)
    substrate           substrate build utilities (package stubbing)
    cache               manage the per-user derivable caches under
                        ~/.uedcli/cache

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --project PROJECT     project root (or its uedcli.toml); else
                        $UEDCLI_PROJECT, else the nearest ancestor dir
                        containing an uedcli.toml walking up from the cwd
uedcli actor:
usage: uedcli actor [-h]
                    {find,show,duplicate,folder,label,build,add,order,delete,bbox,move,prop,rotate,preview}
                    ...

positional arguments:
  {find,show,duplicate,folder,label,build,add,order,delete,bbox,move,prop,rotate,preview}
    find                print names of matching actors (one per line) for
                        piping into name-taking verbs; with no filters, prints
                        every actor
    show                print named actors' full T3D blocks
    duplicate           copy one or more actors (sugar for `actor show <names>
                        | actor add -`): each copy gets a fresh Name, is
                        appended last in CSG order, INHERITS its source's
                        labels, and additionally gets one fresh `dup-<rand>`
                        batch label (so the whole copied batch is re-
                        addressable via `actor find --label dup-<rand>`). A
                        placement is REQUIRED (--by or --at) so copies never
                        silently overlap their originals. Prints the allocated
                        Names to stdout (one per line); the count + batch
                        label go to stderr
    folder              manage an actor's uedcli-side FOLDER: a hierarchical
                        dotted organization path (castle.tower.roof) stored in
                        a trunk sidecar — NOT the T3D Group prop, never
                        emitted to the built map. Sub-verbs: set / unset / get
                        / rename
    label               manage an actor's uedcli-side LABELS: a flat, multi-
                        valued set of classification tokens (lighting,
                        flammable, dup-a1f) stored in a trunk sidecar —
                        orthogonal to the FOLDER path, the T3D Group prop, and
                        the T3D Tag prop, never emitted to the built map. Sub-
                        verbs: add / remove / clear / get. Level-only (rejects
                        --tree stash|prefab)
    build               build a point actor T3D and write to stdout
                        (stateless; no level needed)
    add                 add actors from a T3D file (or - for stdin) to the
                        $UEDCLI_LEVEL's trunk
    order               reorder EXISTING actors' CSG precedence by minting new
                        order_values (no geometry change). CSG order is the
                        (order_value, name) sort; --first makes an actor
                        carve/add BEFORE everything else. Multiple actors move
                        as a block preserving their relative order
    delete              delete one or more actors from $UEDCLI_LEVEL
    bbox                print the world axis-aligned bounding box
                        (min/max/size/center) enclosing the given actors — ONE
                        box over the whole set (a single actor prints its own
                        box; the multi-actor case IS the union, so there is no
                        --union flag: `actor find --folder castle.* | actor
                        bbox -` gives the union). Honours each actor's
                        rotation/scale/location; a point actor contributes a
                        zero-size box at its Location
    move                move a single actor to/by a world coordinate
    prop                read, set, or clear an actor's properties model-side,
                        validated against the actor's class schema (no
                        editor). Sub-verbs: set / unset / get
    rotate              rotate a group of actors around a pivot
                        (PITCH,YAW,ROLL in unreal rotation units, 16384 = 90°)
    preview             self-rendered orthographic wireframe of actors from
                        $UEDCLI_LEVEL (brushes coloured by CSG op; point
                        actors as sprites/markers). Model-side, host-only — no
                        editor

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
uedcli actor find:
usage: uedcli actor find [-h] [--exact-class C] [--subclass-of C] [--group G]
                         [--name GLOB] [--prop KEY[.PATH]=VALUE]
                         [--within-bbox X0,Y0,Z0,X1,Y1,Z1]
                         [--overlapping-bbox X0,Y0,Z0,X1,Y1,Z1]
                         [--kind {point,brush}]
                         [--folder PATTERN | --no-folder]
                         [--label GLOB | --no-label] [--json] [--exclude]
                         [--tree KIND/NAME]
                         [-]

positional arguments:
  -                     the single token - reads a newline-separated actor-
                        name list from stdin and uses THAT set as the universe
                        `find` searches (the filters become a predicate over
                        it): `actor find --group A | actor find --group B -` =
                        A AND B. Omit to search the whole tree.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --exact-class C       match actors whose class is EXACTLY C (bare or fully-
                        qualified Package.Name, case-insensitive) — does NOT
                        include subclasses (`--exact-class Light` skips
                        Spotlight); use --subclass-of for descendant-aware
                        matching. Repeat to OR classes
  --subclass-of C       match actors whose class IS C or DESCENDS from it
                        (e.g. --subclass-of Engine.Light also matches
                        Spotlight, TriggerLight, …) — the descendant-aware
                        class filter, matching `class list --subclass-of`'s
                        spelling. Needs the class schema (the game .u
                        install). Repeat to OR multiple bases; ORs with
                        --exact-class
  --group G             match actors that are members of group G (case-
                        insensitive, comma-joined groups are split — repeat to
                        OR multiple groups)
  --name GLOB           match actors whose Name matches the fnmatch glob GLOB
                        (case-insensitive, whole-name anchored — use wildcards
                        for prefix/substring, e.g. 'Helper*'); repeat to OR
                        multiple patterns
  --prop KEY[.PATH]=VALUE
                        match actors on the EFFECTIVE value of KEY (dot-paths
                        reach array elements and struct members, e.g.
                        Location.X=512): the stored value if present, else the
                        class default decoded from the game packages;
                        comparison is type-aware (True==1, 4==4.0, enum
                        name==ordinal). An actor whose class does not declare
                        KEY simply does not match; a KEY no considered class
                        declares errors. Needs the class schema (the game .u
                        install). Repeat to AND multiple props
  --within-bbox X0,Y0,Z0,X1,Y1,Z1
                        match actors whose world bounding box is FULLY INSIDE
                        the given axis-aligned box — two opposite corners in
                        any order, unreal units (same space as --at), edge-
                        inclusive. Honours each actor's full transform (a
                        scaled/rotated brush's TRUE world box is tested); a
                        point actor (Light, mesh deco, nav point) is its
                        Location point. Single-valued; ANDs with the other
                        filters. Selects a region's actors to pipe into a set
                        verb (add --kind brush for geometry only, e.g. `…
                        --within-bbox … --kind brush | actor preview -`).
  --overlapping-bbox X0,Y0,Z0,X1,Y1,Z1
                        match actors whose world bounding box OVERLAPS the
                        given axis-aligned box (a straddling brush that poked
                        out of --within-bbox IS caught) — two opposite corners
                        in any order, unreal units, edge-inclusive. Honours
                        each actor's full transform; a point actor is its
                        Location point. Single-valued; ANDs with the other
                        filters. NOTE this tests the world AABB, so a
                        diagonal/L-shaped brush can match on its bounding box
                        without any solid geometry actually inside the box (a
                        precise per-poly variant is not implemented — board
                        item find-relational-predicates).
  --kind {point,brush}  Filter by actor kind: 'brush' = actors that carry
                        brush geometry (a PolyList — CSG brushes, builders,
                        movers; the ones brush/poly/vertex verbs accept);
                        'point' = location-only actors with no brush (Light,
                        LevelInfo, navigation points, AND mesh decorations — a
                        mesh deco has visible geometry but is still a point
                        actor). This is the brush-vs-point split, not 'has any
                        geometry'. Distinct from --exact-class/--subclass-of,
                        which match the UnrealScript class name. Omit to match
                        both kinds.
  --folder PATTERN      match actors by uedcli-side folder (globstar): a
                        WILDCARD-FREE pattern like 'castle' selects that
                        folder AND its WHOLE SUBTREE (so bare = subtree —
                        there is no short form for 'just the castle node');
                        '*' = exactly one segment; '**' = any depth (zero+).
                        NOTE the subtree/glob asymmetry: a WILDCARDED pattern
                        is a pure glob with NO subtree extension — '**.roof'
                        matches roof NODES only, not their contents (use
                        --folder '**.roof' --folder '**.roof.**' for 'every
                        roof and everything inside'). Case-insensitive;
                        '?'/'['/']' are rejected. Repeat to OR patterns; ANDs
                        with --exact-class/--subclass-of/--group/--name/--kind
  --no-folder           match only UNFOLDERED actors (folder unset) — the ONLY
                        way to query them, since a None folder matches no
                        --folder pattern. Mutually exclusive with --folder
  --label GLOB          match actors by uedcli-side label (flat `*`-glob): an
                        actor matches if ANY of its labels matches GLOB. `*`
                        is the ONLY wildcard ('dup-*' finds a duplicate batch,
                        'lighting' matches that exact label); '?'/'['/']' are
                        rejected. Case-insensitive. Repeat to OR patterns;
                        ANDs with --exact-class/--subclass-
                        of/--group/--name/--kind/--folder
  --no-label            match only UNLABELLED actors (empty label set) — the
                        ONLY way to query them, since an unlabelled actor
                        matches no --label pattern. Mutually exclusive with
                        --label
  --json                print the matching names as a JSON array instead of
                        one name per line (for scripts that want structured
                        output)
  --exclude             with -, keep the piped actors that do NOT match the
                        filters instead of those that do (set difference):
                        `find --group A | find --group B --exclude -` = A but
                        not B. Requires -.
  --tree KIND/NAME      operate on this tree instead of $UEDCLI_LEVEL:
                        KIND/NAME where KIND is level|stash|prefab and NAME is
                        the level/stash/prefab name (may be nested, e.g.
                        stash/hangar/arch). Default: the level named by
                        $UEDCLI_LEVEL.
uedcli actor show:
usage: uedcli actor show [-h] [--t3d-only] [--tree KIND/NAME] name

positional arguments:
  name              ONE actor Name (case-insensitive; NOT a glob — `actor
                    find` owns patterns), or - to read a newline-separated
                    name list from stdin (e.g. `actor find 'Light*' | actor
                    show -`; concatenated blocks in piped order). A name that
                    matches no actor errors (exit 2); empty stdin is a clean
                    no-op (exit 0)

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --t3d-only        suppress the `// uedcli-folder:` comment for a byte-exact
                    editor export (rarely needed). By DEFAULT each foldered
                    block carries the comment — importable into UnrealEd
                    unchanged (it silently strips bare `//` lines) AND round-
                    trips the folder through `actor show A | actor add -`
  --tree KIND/NAME  operate on this tree instead of $UEDCLI_LEVEL: KIND/NAME
                    where KIND is level|stash|prefab and NAME is the
                    level/stash/prefab name (may be nested, e.g.
                    stash/hangar/arch). Default: the level named by
                    $UEDCLI_LEVEL.
uedcli actor duplicate:
usage: uedcli actor duplicate [-h] (--by DX,DY,DZ | --at X,Y,Z) [--label L]
                              [--folder PATH] [--tree KIND/NAME]
                              names [names ...]

positional arguments:
  names             actor Names (case-insensitive) to duplicate, or the single
                    token - to read a newline-separated name list from stdin
                    (e.g. `actor find … | actor duplicate -`); - is the sole
                    source, not mixable with names

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --by DX,DY,DZ     world delta added to EACH copy's Location (relative
                    offset; preserves the set's relative layout)
  --at X,Y,Z        anchor the copied set's bounding-box minimum corner at
                    this world coordinate (the whole set shifts together,
                    preserving relative layout)
  --label L         an extra label token stamped on every copy IN ADDITION to
                    the inherited labels and the fresh dup-<rand> batch token;
                    repeat for many
  --folder PATH     place the copies in this uedcli-side folder path
                    (overrides each original's folder); omit to keep each
                    original's folder
  --tree KIND/NAME  operate on this tree instead of $UEDCLI_LEVEL: KIND/NAME
                    where KIND is level|stash|prefab and NAME is the
                    level/stash/prefab name (may be nested, e.g.
                    stash/hangar/arch). Default: the level named by
                    $UEDCLI_LEVEL.
uedcli actor folder:
usage: uedcli actor folder [-h] {set,unset,get,rename} ...

positional arguments:
  {set,unset,get,rename}
    set                 assign a folder path to one or more actors (validate-
                        all before any write; all sidecars land or none do).
                        Echoes touched Names to stdout
    unset               clear the folder (remove the sidecar file) on one or
                        more actors. Echoes touched Names to stdout
    get                 print each actor's folder path, one line per actor in
                        argument order; an unfoldered actor prints `(none)`
    rename              re-parent/rename a whole folder subtree: rewrite every
                        actor filed at OLD or under it (OLD and OLD.*) so its
                        OLD prefix becomes NEW. `castle.tower` also moves
                        `castle.tower.roof`. Folders have no existence apart
                        from the actors filed in them, so this is purely a
                        bulk sidecar rewrite. Prints the touched actor Names
                        to stdout, the count to stderr. Trunk-only (rejects
                        --tree stash|prefab).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
uedcli actor folder set:
usage: uedcli actor folder set [-h] --to PATH [--tree KIND/NAME]
                               names [names ...]

options:

                    insensitively
  --tree KIND/NAME  operate on this tree instead of $UEDCLI_LEVEL: KIND/NAME

uedcli actor build:
usage: uedcli actor build [-h] [--at X,Y,Z] [--base-name BASE_NAME]
                          [--prop KEY[.PATH]=VALUE] [--rotate PITCH,YAW,ROLL]
                          [--folder PATH] [--label L]
                          Package.Class

positional arguments:
  Package.Class         fully-qualified actor class, e.g. Engine.Light

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --at X,Y,Z            world Location (default origin)
  --base-name BASE_NAME
                        base Name (stem) for the emitted actor; a unique
                        `_<rand>` suffix is appended at `actor add`, so this
                        is a prefix, not the final Name (default: the class
                        name, e.g. Light). Give distinct base names when
                        batching several `actor build`s so `actor add` keeps
                        them all.
  --prop KEY[.PATH]=VALUE
                        extra actor property (repeat for multiple), schema-
                        validated against the class before emit — same grammar
                        as `actor prop set` (dot-paths, array tuple form,
                        Vector/Rotator comma sugar); member edits compose onto
                        the class default
  --rotate PITCH,YAW,ROLL
                        SET the emitted actor's Rotation field to this
                        ABSOLUTE orientation in unreal rotation units (16384 =
                        90°, 65536 = a full turn; a fresh generated actor
                        starts at identity, so no add-vs-override ambiguity).
                        Convenience shorthand for --prop
                        Rotation=PITCH,YAW,ROLL
  --folder PATH         hierarchical organization PATH (dotted, e.g.
                        castle.wall.north) for the emitted actor — a uedcli-
                        side sidecar, NEVER emitted to the built map, rides
                        the T3D as a `// uedcli-folder:` carrier that `actor
                        add` persists.
  --label L             cross-cutting classification label for the emitted
                        actor (repeat for several) — a uedcli-side sidecar,
                        NEVER emitted to the built map, rides the T3D as a `//
                        uedcli-labels:` carrier `actor add` persists.
uedcli actor add:
usage: uedcli actor add [-h] [--order POS] [--tree KIND/NAME] file

positional arguments:
  file              T3D snippet file, or - to read from stdin

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --order POS       CSG-order placement of the added actor(s): first | last
                    (default) | before=NAME | after=NAME. `first` mints an
                    order_value below every existing actor (lowest CSG order,
                    carves first); before=/after=NAME places adjacent to NAME.
                    Multiple actors added at once land as a block preserving
                    their input order. Level target only (rejected on --tree
                    stash|prefab, which have no order_value sidecar)
  --tree KIND/NAME  operate on this tree instead of $UEDCLI_LEVEL: KIND/NAME
                    where KIND is level|stash|prefab and NAME is the
                    level/stash/prefab name (may be nested, e.g.
                    stash/hangar/arch). Default: the level named by
                    $UEDCLI_LEVEL.
uedcli actor order:
usage: uedcli actor order [-h]
                          (--first | --last | --before NAME | --after NAME)
                          [--tree KIND/NAME]
                          names [names ...]

positional arguments:
  names             actor Names to reorder (case-insensitive), or the single
                    token - to read a newline-separated name list from stdin
                    (e.g. `actor find … | actor order - --first`); - is the
                    sole source, not mixable with names

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --first           place before the current LOWEST CSG order (new minimum —
                    carves first)
  --last            place after the current HIGHEST CSG order (new maximum)
  --before NAME     place immediately before NAME in CSG order (NAME must

  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --from-t3d FILE [FILE ...]

                        spiral | actor preview --from-t3d -`). Multiple files
                        concatenate in order; - is the sole value if present.
                        Mutually exclusive with the names source
  --layout {quad,single,breakdown}
                        pane layout (default quad). 'quad' = the UED-style 2x2
                        grid (Top / Front / Iso / Side). 'single' = one view,
                        per --view. 'breakdown' = a near-square GRID that
                        walks the scene actor by actor: pane 0 is the whole
                        scene in CSG colour (a plain spatial map — no legend,
                        names or numbers), then ONE focused + zoomed pane per
                        actor — a brush with all its faces numbered and
                        captioned, a point actor with its marker/sprite
                        captioned. breakdown uses --view and sets its OWN per-
                        pane focus/zoom, so --frame/--focus are ignored under
                        it
  --view {top,front,side,iso}
                        which single view 'single'/'breakdown' render (ignored
                        by 'quad', which shows all four); 'iso' separates

  --iso-angle ISO_ANGLE
                        iso receding-edge angle from horizontal (default 30°)
  --faces {wire,textured}
                        how brush faces are drawn (default 'wire'). 'wire' =
                        outlines only, the content-free schematic — CSG-
                        coloured (added blue, subtracted gold, …), needs no
                        game install. 'textured' = the CSG-solved textured
                        world, as UnrealEd's 3D viewport draws it: runs the
                        native CSG solve over the set and fills only the
                        surfaces that survive, each through its real texture
                        and authored UV frame (Origin/TextureU/TextureV/Pan),
                        NO wireframe — so alignment, panning and tiling are
                        visible offline (no editor, no lighting). An additive
                        brush not inside subtracted space is invisible; a
                        solve that leaves nothing exits 2. 'textured' needs a
                        resolved project, the per-user games config and every
                        referenced texture readable, and rejects --brush-
                        colors and any scaled or sheared brush; 'wire' needs
                        none of that and works on --from-t3d from anywhere
  --brush-colors {csg,legend}
                        how to colour the '--faces wire' wireframe: 'csg' (the
                        default) = by CSG op (added blue, subtracted gold,
                        semisolid pink, nonsolid green, mover magenta);
                        'legend' = each brush in its own per-actor tint (drops
                        the CSG cue but tells same-op brushes apart at a
                        glance). Rejected under --faces textured (which
                        samples real textures, colouring nothing from this
                        flag)
  --annotate ANNOTATE   comma-set of poly-index selectors (union). Bare 'poly'
                        = every face index; colon FILTERs narrow; commas
                        union. poly filters: vis (inert alias of bare poly —
                        on-face numbering is facing-blind), hi (highlighted
                        faces only; 'highlighted' is an accepted synonym).
                        e.g. 'poly:hi' = highlighted faces only; 'poly:vis' =
                        every face index (same as bare poly). Keywords (stand
                        alone): none, all (=poly), highlighted (=poly:hi).

                        — locate a brush by its grid cell (printed on stderr)
  --frame TARGET        frame a target to fill the view; frames ONLY, does NOT
                        highlight. Two forms: a SELECTOR — a bare BRUSH name
                        frames that actor's whole AABB, or BRUSH:IDX (the
                        selector `brush poly find` prints) frames ONE poly (a
                        multi-index / `:all` value is an error — use
                        --highlight for a set); OR an explicit world AABB —
                        six comma-separated numbers X0,Y0,Z0,X1,Y1,Z1, framed
                        exactly. Not applied under --layout breakdown, which
                        frames each pane itself (a value is still validated)
  --frame-tightness N   framing tightness toward a --frame SELECTOR target: 0
                        = no zoom (whole-set frame), 1 = tightest (target + a
                        small margin), in between interpolates; must be in
                        [0,1]. Default 0.8. No --frame ⇒ no-op. An explicit
                        AABB --frame is always framed exactly, unaffected by
                        this
  --highlight POLY|NAME
                        emphasise a poly or an actor; repeatable, no effect on
                        framing. A token WITH a colon is a poly selector
                        BRUSH:IDX (the set form BRUSH:1,2 and BRUSH:all work
                        too) — those polys draw with a bolder line in their
                        brush's vivid CSG hue; under --faces textured the
                        highlighted face keeps its texture and takes only that
                        vivid outline. It re-colours what is VISIBLE and never
                        x-rays: a face hidden behind something at this --view
                        draws nothing. A stderr note names any selector that
                        ended up not visible for ANY reason — hidden, culled,
                        or outside the frame. A token WITHOUT a colon is an
                        ACTOR NAME: a brush actor highlights ALL its polys; a
                        point actor gets corner brackets (a selection reticle)
                        framing its sprite/marker
  --focus BRUSH         spotlight ONE brush: only it shows face indices (in
                        its label tint); every OTHER brush recedes — its
                        wireframe to faint (dimmed) lines, and under --faces
                        textured its solved fills to a faint wash of their own
                        colour. It changes BRIGHTNESS ONLY, never what is
                        visible or what hides what: a brush between the camera
                        and the focused one still covers it. All actor names
                        still appear in the legend. --highlight OVERRIDES this
                        — a highlighted poly/actor stays vivid+bold and
                        undimmed and keeps its index even when its brush is
                        not the focus — but it does not x-ray: a highlighted
                        face that something in front of it hides draws
                        nothing. An unknown name / a point actor → clean exit
                        2. Not applied under --layout breakdown, which focuses
                        each pane itself (a value is still validated)
  --show SET            comma-set (union) of range overlays to draw for POINT
                        actors (default none): 'collision' = a faint light-red
                        collision cylinder for every colliding point actor
                        (bCollideActors true) — a circle in TOP, a 2·radius ×
                        2·height rect in FRONT/SIDE, an 8-sided wire cylinder
                        in ISO; 'light-range' = a faint orange sphere of a

                        does look classes up, but only to tell a mover (drawn
                        as a magenta overlay) from a world brush — it draws no
                        extra overlay
  --size PX             output image edge length in pixels (default 1024)
  --grid N              density of the always-on addressable grid: N columns
                        (A,B,C…) across the top and N rows (1,2,3…) down both
                        sides, so every region of the image has a text
                        address. Each actor's cell is reported on stderr (and

uedcli texture list:
usage: uedcli texture list [-h] [--package PACKAGE] [--group G] [--masked]
                           [--classified | --unclassified] [--json]
                           [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --package PACKAGE     restrict to this package (bare stem)
  --group G             keep only textures whose group (Outer) is G, e.g.
                        Ladder
  --masked              keep only textures whose effective bMasked flag is
                        true (decodes each to read the flag)
  --classified          keep only textures whose content identity has a
                        classification shard
  --unclassified        keep only textures with NO shard yet — the worklist
  --json                emit one JSON object per texture (JSONL): {ref,
                        identity, classified, group, masked, preview} where
                        preview is a cached path or null (list NEVER renders)
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)
uedcli texture show:
usage: uedcli texture show [-h] [--json] [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]
                           [Package[.Group].Name ...]

positional arguments:

                        list from stdin

options:

  --json                print one JSON object per ref {ref, width, height,
                        format, group, masked, identity, colors,
                        classification} instead of the text block
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)
uedcli texture preview:
usage: uedcli texture preview [-h] [--out PATH] [--skeleton]
                              [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]
                              [Package[.Group].Name ...]

positional arguments:
  Package[.Group].Name  texture ref(s) to render, or - to read a newline ref
                        list from stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out PATH            host path to write the PNG to (relative → cwd); the
                        extension is replaced by .png. With no --out a unique
                        temp file is minted. With several refs the LAST
                        written path wins a fixed --out.
  --skeleton            stream a ready-to-fill JSONL row per ref {ref,
                        preview, tags:[], description:'', colors:[…]} (colours
                        pre-filled from the pixels) instead of the
                        `<ref><TAB><path>` line — pipe it into `classify set
                        -`
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)
uedcli texture search:
usage: uedcli texture search [-h] [--tag TAG] [--color C] [--package PACKAGE]
                             [--group G] [--masked]
                             [--classified | --unclassified] [--json]
                             [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]
                             [TERM ...]

positional arguments:
  TERM                  one or more search terms (case-insensitive); a texture
                        must match EVERY term. At least one is required (term-
                        less exits 2 → `list`).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tag TAG             keep only textures carrying this exact stored tag
                        (repeat to AND)
  --color C             keep only textures whose colours include C — stored
                        colours for a classified texture, else derived live
                        from pixels (repeat to OR). Must be a palette name.
  --package PACKAGE     restrict to this package (bare stem)
  --group G             restrict to group G
  --masked              keep only masked textures
  --classified          keep only classified textures
  --unclassified        keep only unclassified textures
  --json                emit one JSON object per match (JSONL), best first:
                        {ref, score, classified, tags, description, colors}
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)

uedcli texture classify:
usage: uedcli texture classify [-h] {set,unset,status,tags} ...

positional arguments:
  {set,unset,status,tags}
    set                 record a texture's classification against its content
                        identity. Over an EXISTING shard it REFUSES (exit 2
                        naming it); --force REPLACES it wholesale (no tag
                        union). The single token - reads JSONL rows {ref,
                        tags?, description?, colors?} from stdin (validate-
                        all-then-write; empty stdin is a clean no-op, exit 0).
    unset               undo classification on one or more textures (by their
                        content identity). Any of --tags[=A,B] / --description
                        / --colors / --all (combine field clears; --all
                        deletes the whole shard). The single token - reads a
                        newline ref list from stdin (empty stdin is a clean
                        no-op, exit 0).
    status              classification progress: how many textures on the path
                        have a shard, of the total. --json for a machine
                        object.
    tags                the tag vocabulary in use across all shards, with
                        occurrence counts (curbs drift). Reads only the shard
                        tree, so --catalog-dir runs it outside a project.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
uedcli texture classify set:
usage: uedcli texture classify set [-h] [--tags A,B]
                                   [--description DESCRIPTION] [--colors A,B]
                                   [--force] [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]
                                   [Package[.Group].Name]

positional arguments:
  Package[.Group].Name  the texture to classify, or - to read JSONL rows from
                        stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tags A,B            comma list of tags (strip/lowercase/de-dupe
                        normalized)
  --description DESCRIPTION
                        prose description
  --colors A,B          comma list of palette colour names, OVERRIDING the
                        pixel pre-fill (unknown names exit 2). Omit to keep
                        the derived colours.
  --force               replace an existing classification for this identity
                        instead of exiting 2 (wholesale — no tag union; also
                        governs each JSONL row under -)
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)
uedcli texture classify unset:
usage: uedcli texture classify unset [-h]
                                     (--tags [A,B] | --description | --colors | --all)
                                     [--catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR]
                                     [Package[.Group].Name ...]

positional arguments:
  Package[.Group].Name  texture(s) to unset, or - to read a newline ref list
                        from stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --tags [A,B]          remove the named tags (comma list); BARE --tags clears
                        the whole field
  --description         clear the description field
  --colors              clear the colour override (search falls back to live-
                        derive)
  --all                 delete the whole shard (the only full clear)
  --catalog-dir CATALOG_DIR
                        tracked classification-shard dir (default: the
                        resolved project's catalog dir — the uedcli.toml
                        `catalog` key, or <root>/texture-catalog/)

uedcli cache:
usage: uedcli cache [-h] {clear,gc} ...

positional arguments:
  {clear,gc}
    clear     delete the persistent package-schema cache
              (~/.uedcli/cache/schema); it is pure derivable throwaway and
              rebuilds on the next command. Use for the schema-cache escape-
              hatch/paranoid case or to reclaim old decoder-version (v<N>/)
              dirs.
    gc        shrink the package-schema cache without emptying it: delete the
              orphaned old decoder-version (v<N>/) dirs, then evict current-
              version entries least-recently-used until the cache fits its
              size/count cap. Cached entries are derivable, so an evicted one
              simply re-decodes the next time it is needed. Runs automatically
              (best-effort) after a cache write; this is the on-demand
              surface.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
uedcli cache clear:
usage: uedcli cache clear [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
uedcli cache gc:
usage: uedcli cache gc [-h] [--max-bytes N] [--max-entries N]

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --max-bytes N    evict until the cache holds at most N bytes (default: the
                   built-in cap, 256 MiB, or $UEDCLI_SCHEMA_CACHE_MAX_BYTES).
                   0 evicts everything.
  --max-entries N  evict until the cache holds at most N blob files (default:
                   no count cap unless $UEDCLI_SCHEMA_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES sets
                   one). 0 evicts everything.
